Subject: Horizon AI - spike reconciliation & next steps

Hi Olivia / Tom,

Thanks again for the time last week — I pulled together a short usage snapshot attached (Horizon_Usage_Report_Mar_Apr_2027.csv) showing the two-day spike we discussed. From our side it looks like ~420k additional inference hours landed between Mar 16-17 due to the bulk predictions job you mentioned.

I want to get this reconciled quickly and keep you running smoothly. Two immediate options to consider:

- One-off make-good credit to offset the overage on the Mar invoice
- Convert a portion of the overage into a 3-month roll-forward of capacity (credits applied to future months) with a modest discount for the conversion

Before we pick a path, can you confirm whether Horizon would prefer a credit now (simple), or to convert to committed capacity (helps avoid future spikes)? If you want, Neha can do a short breakdown of per-day usage and token distribution so we can nail the exact overage window.

I’m available Thu 10–11am PT for a quick call.

Thanks,

Thanks Ben — appreciate the fast turnaround and the report.

Short context: we ran an ad-hoc batch re-score across a 6M-row backlog on Mar 16 that unintentionally hit production models instead of the offline replica. That caused the spike. We own the mistake; that said, the invoice impact is material for our finance team this quarter.

Two asks from Horizon:
1) Can you share a per-day breakdown for the Mar window (we need the line items for our internal chargeback)?
2) Our CFO would prefer a blended remediation: a partial credit now plus the remainder amortized across the next two billing cycles, ideally with some committed capacity added to avoid recurrence.

If you and Neha can put the numbers together (breakdown + proposal), we’ll route to finance. We’re free Thu afternoon PT.

—Olivia
Olivia Barnes

Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Horizon AI - spike reconciliation & next steps

Hi Olivia / Tom — attaching the per-day breakout you requested and a short proposed remediation term sheet (Draft_Makegood_Term_Sheet.pdf). Quick summary of the findings:

- Confirmed overage window: Mar 16 00:00 - Mar 17 23:59 PT
- Total additional inference hours: 423,812 (billed as overage)
- Peak hour concentrated around Mar 16 10:00–12:00 when the batch hit prod models

Proposed remediation (two-track, as discussed):

1) Immediate one-time credit = 30% of the overage charge (applied to the Apr invoice)
2) Amortize the remaining 70% across the next two billing cycles (May & Jun) as a staged payment
3) Include a 3-month reserved burst pool equivalent to 150k hours at 12% off list price; contract addendum to cover term details

Rationale: the credit acknowledges Horizon’s operational mitigation while the amortization avoids a single large cash hit. The reserved burst pool gives you headroom and reduces future overage risk. If Horizon prefers a lump-sum credit instead, we can move to a 45% one-time credit and skip amortization.

I’ve put numbers in the attached term sheet and included line-item math for your finance team. Ben — I recommend we offer the staged option as our primary path; it’s conservative for Redwood and easier to accept for Horizon. Marissa — I’ve flagged this for approval of the credit/opportunity to upsell to committed capacity.

Next steps: Olivia, tell us which option (staged vs larger lump sum) Horizon prefers and we’ll issue an amendment + credit memo. If you want to discuss, we’re available Thu 2–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0177
